textLayout.text: Reliable control enables action
Evidence-grounded PID and Fuzzy-PID evaluation for a 2-link manipulator

slides.title: Nominal success does not prove reliable manipulation

textLayout.text: Nominal success does not prove reliable manipulation
Controller choice must survive changes in payload, configuration, noise, disturbance, and actuator authority.

A controller can pass one nominal trajectory and still fail when uncertainties interact.

This study therefore reports failed completed runs instead of filtering them from averages.

All conclusions are simulation-only; no hardware safety or fidelity claim is made.

Manual PID, Mamdani Fuzzy-PID, and optimized PID use identical robot parameters, torque limits, trajectories, thresholds, and random seeds.

slides.title: Optimization improves PID under a fixed protocol

textLayout.text: Optimization improves PID under a fixed protocol
Optimization lowers the nominal objective 7.283% and the held-out payload objective from 0.214504 to 0.197284.

The search converges with exit flag 1 after 12 iterations and 96 evaluations.

Only PID gains change; the plant, torque limits, trajectory, objective, and evaluation thresholds remain fixed.
Deterministic stress separates controller reliability
Success rises from 8/13 for manual PID to 9/13 for Fuzzy-PID and 10/13 for optimized PID.

The matrix contains 39 controller-scenario runs across nominal, payload, configuration, uncertainty, disturbance, actuator, and combined conditions.

All 3 controllers fail the combined deterministic case, so the ranking is comparative rather than a safety guarantee.

slides.title: Noise alone is manageable; combined stress is not

textLayout.text: Noise alone is manageable; combined stress is not
Each isolated-noise cell passes 30/30 paired trials, while every combined-stress cell passes 0/30.

Study: 360 trials (4 scenarios x 3 controllers x 30 fixed seeds).

At high noise, optimized PID has the lowest tracking error but the highest mean torque slew (2888.34 N m/s).
Task-space tests expose hidden failures
All 3 controllers pass straight-line; only optimized PID passes pick-transfer-place, so 4 of 6 task runs pass every gate.

Manual and Fuzzy-PID complete the pick-transfer-place simulation but fail its quantitative pickup/place criteria.

Optimized PID records 0.01422 m RMS and 0.02970 m maximum Cartesian error.

Nominal metrics are mixed across manual PID and Fuzzy-PID; optimized PID provides the best aggregate deterministic and Cartesian reliability, with a torque-slew trade-off under noise.

slides.title: Validated layer supports the next research step

textLayout.text: Validated layer supports the next research step
The next milestone is to test whether the same evidence discipline survives contact with sensing, hardware uncertainty, and online safety constraints.

1. Hardware-in-the-loop and physical-arm validation with calibrated uncertainty.

2. Perception and task-planning integration above the existing inner-loop controller layer.

3. Online monitoring, collision avoidance, and explicit safety supervision before deployment.
